## Source and method

- https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics
- https://github.com/stevenzchen/pose-trainer
- https://github.com/NgoQuocBao1010/Exercise-Correction
- https://github.com/thphuc05/PythonExcercisePoseEstimation

The joint-angle and ratio thresholds that 4 licensed open-source exercise trackers (Ultralytics AIGym (workouts monitoring solution), AGPL-3.0; Pose Trainer (Steven Chen and Richard Yang), GPL-3.0; Exercise-Correction (Ngô Hồng Quốc Bảo), MIT; PythonExcercisePoseEstimation (thphuc05), MIT) use to count reps, check form and time holds, read from their code on 2026-11-05. Every value was captured by the generator from the verbatim line in "quote", after that line was found in the fetched file; "usage" is the line that applies it and "measureQuote" the line that computes what it is compared with, both checked the same way. Values are null where no source read states a number, with the reason in nullReason. These are the projects' own choices for their own camera setups and models, measured as 2D angles in the image; they are not biomechanical standards, coaching or medical advice. The sources' own code is under their licenses; this dataset quotes single lines of it as evidence.

## Fields

| Field | Description | JSON types | Null in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | Stable row id | string | 0 of 25 rows |
| `exercise` | Exercise slug | string | 0 of 25 rows |
| `exerciseName` | Exercise name | string | 0 of 25 rows |
| `purpose` | rep-count (a phase boundary), form-check (an error rule) or hold (an isometric rule) | string | 0 of 25 rows |
| `role` | top, bottom, depth, range, minimum, maximum, lockout, frames, or top-and-bottom for a null rep-count row | string | 0 of 25 rows |
| `measure` | joint-angle, segment-angle, range-of-motion, ratio or frames | string | 0 of 25 rows |
| `joint` | The joint or quantity measured | null, string | 1 of 25 rows |
| `points` | The points as the source names them, vertex in the middle for a three-point angle | null, string | 2 of 25 rows |
| `keypointIndices` | COCO 17 indices where the source names indices; resolved to names through this site's keypoint dataset | null, string | 23 of 25 rows |
| `comparison` | How the source compares the measured value with the threshold (>, <, >=, <=, within) | null, string | 3 of 25 rows |
| `value` | The threshold, captured from quote; null where no source states one | integer, null, number | 3 of 25 rows |
| `value2` | Upper bound of a within range | integer, null, number | 23 of 25 rows |
| `unit` | degrees, ratio or frames | string | 0 of 25 rows |
| `meaning` | What crossing the value does in the source (this site's wording; usage is the evidence) | string | 0 of 25 rows |
| `sourceProject` | The project the value was read from | null, string | 1 of 25 rows |
| `sourceRepo` | Its repository | null, string | 1 of 25 rows |
| `license` | Its license, as its LICENSE file states | null, string | 1 of 25 rows |
| `source` | The file and line on GitHub | null, string | 1 of 25 rows |
| `quote` | The verbatim line the value was captured from | null, string | 3 of 25 rows |
| `usage` | The verbatim line that applies the value | null, string | 3 of 25 rows |
| `measureQuote` | The verbatim line that computes the measured quantity | null, string | 3 of 25 rows |
| `reasonQuote` | For a null row: the verbatim line that shows why the source states no number | null, string | 23 of 25 rows |
| `nullReason` | Why the value is null | null, string | 22 of 25 rows |
| `page` | This site's row | string | 0 of 25 rows |

A null means the source does not state the value or it could not be verified. It never means zero, and it is never a guess. In the CSV a null is an empty unquoted field.

## Update cadence

- `src/data/formRules.ts` is generated by `scripts/fetch-form-rules.mjs` from the sources above, last read 2026-11-05.
- No workflow runs that script: it is run by hand when the sources are re-read.
- The files are rebuilt by `npm run datasets` (scripts/build-datasets.mjs); a run with no source change writes byte-identical files. The edition stays 2026.1, and a new edition ships under a new file name rather than overwriting this one.
